title: Lead 1: labor headcount vs score (opponent-vs-opponent natural experiment + causal test)

natural_experiment.source: Replays/Auto/leaderboard-* (200 files, 400 seat-rows), verified zero graceyunliu participants

melon_rate_vs_final_money.note: no correlation -- corroborates Phase 4B/7 causal nulls

causal_test.change: _load_model() hire-target forced +3 above the policy's own computed target, funded from the same cash trajectory (not free hands). Single-line change.
causal_test.design_rationale: Explicitly addresses the cash-confound the coordinator raised: if hands have independent causal value, spending more of the SAME budget on them should help; if the correlation just reflects richer play affording both, forcing extra hands should be neutral or negative.
causal_test.conclusion: No significant score effect in any test. The confound is not ruled out in headcount's favor -- forcing extra hands from the same budget does not reliably improve score, consistent with headcount being a side effect of successful play rather than a cause of it.

recommendation: None. Not confirmed as a causal lead.
